'''Jiří Patera''' (10 October 1936 – 3 January 2022) was a Czech-born Canadian mathematician and academic.<ref name="CRM">{{cite web|url=http://www.crm.umontreal.ca/pdf/JiriPatera1936-2022FRA.pdf|title=In memoriam – Jiří Patera (1936–2022)|work=Centre de Recherches Mathématiques|language=French|access-date=16 January 2022|archive-date=21 January 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220121134842/http://www.crm.umontreal.ca/pdf/JiriPatera1936-2022FRA.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref> He taught at the [[Université de Montréal]] and was known for his work in [[group theory]], [[Lie group]]s, and [[cryptography]].

==Life and career==
Patera attended secondary school in [[Děčín]] and subsequently studied [[theoretical physics]] at [[Moscow State University]]. There he met and married [https://mellenpress.com/author/tatiana-a-patera/4809/ Tatiana Chalnikova].  In 1964, he earned a doctorate from [[Charles University]], pursued a postdoc at the [[Université de Montréal|University of Montreal]] and returned to Prague in 1966.  In August 1968, with [https://history.state.gov/milestones/1961-1968/soviet-invasion-czechoslavkia Soviet tanks rolling into Czechoslovakia], he emigrated with Tatiana and their daughter first to the UK and finally settling in [[Montreal]], Canada, a year later.  He joined the [[Université de Montréal|Universite de Montreal]] as an assistant professor and then newly created [http://www.crm.umontreal.ca/en/index.shtml Centre de Recherches Mathematiques] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220214175236/http://www.crm.umontreal.ca/en/index.shtml |date=14 February 2022 }} at the university.

Patera began his work in group theory and Lie groups. From 1965 to 1972, he published several works on constructive theories of the representation of compact Lie groups. In 1981, he published ''Tables de dimensions, d'indices et de règles de branchement pour les représentations d'algèbres de Lie simples'' and began collaborating with [[Robert Moody]] in the field the following year.

Patera was known for his work on constructive computation prior to the use of [[software engineering]]. He wrote a book on [[Lie algebra representation]]<ref>{{cite book |last1=Patera|first1=Jiří|last2=Sankoff|first2=David|date=1973|title=Branching rules for representations of simple Lie algebras|trans-title= |url= |language= |location=Montreal|publisher=Presses Université de Montréal|isbn=0-8405-0228-1}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Patera|first1=Jiří|last2=McKay|first2=W. G.|date=1981|title=Tables of dimensions, indices, and branching rules for representations of simple Lie algebras|trans-title= |url= |language= |location=New York|publisher=Marcel Dekker|isbn=0-8247-1227-7}}</ref> and primarily worked alongside Robert Moody and [[Hans Zassenhaus]].<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/bulletin-of-the-american-mathematical-society-new-series/volume-7/issue-1/Fast-recursion-formula-for-weight-multiplicities/bams/1183549053.pdf|title=Fast recursion formula for weight multiplicities|journal=American Mathematical Society|year=1982|doi=10.1090/S0273-0979-1982-15021-2|last1=Moody|first1=R. V.|last2=Patera|first2=J.|volume=7|issue=1|pages=237–242|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Patera|first1=Jiří|last2=Moody|first2=Robert|last3=Bremner|first3=Murray|date=1983|title=Tables of dominant weight multiplicities for representations of simple Lie algebras|trans-title= |url= |language= |location=New York|publisher=Marcel Dekker|isbn=0-8247-7270-9}}</ref>

He died in Montreal on 3 January 2022, at the age of 85 with Tatiana at his bedside.<ref name="CRM"/>

==Awards==
*[[Canada Council]] Killam Fellowship (1991)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://recherche.umontreal.ca/english/our-researchers/professors-directory/researcher/is/in14449/|title=Jiri Patera|work=Université de Montréal|language=French}}</ref>
*Algebraic Methods in Physics: Symposium on the 60th Birthday of Jiří Patera and Pavel Winternitz (1997)<ref>{{cite book |last1=Patera|first1=Jiří|last2=Winternitz|first2=Pavel|last3=Saint-Aubin|first3=Yvan|last4=Vinet|first4=Luc|date=2001|title=Algebraic Methods in Physics: A Symposium for the 60th Birthday of Jiří Patera and Pavel Winternitz|trans-title= |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=GL6uPBDZN-AC&q=Symposium+for+the+60th+Birthday+of+Ji%C5%99%C3%AD+Patera+and+Pavel+Winternitz|language= |location=Berlin|publisher=Springer Science & Business Media|isbn=9780387951256}}</ref>
*[[CAP-CRM Prize in Theoretical and Mathematical Physics]] (2004)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://services.cap.ca/awards/press/2004-Patera-f.html|title=Médaille de l'ACP 2004|date=20 April 2004|work=Canadian Association of Physicists|language=French}}</ref>
*Doctor ''honoris causa'' of the [[Czech Technical University in Prague]] (2005)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://notes.math.ca/archives/Notesv37n7.pdf|title=Prix/Distinctions|work=CMS Notes / Notes de la SMC}}</ref>

==Works==
*''Branching rules for representations of simple Lie algebras'' (1971)
*''Tables of dimensions, indices, and branching rules for representations of simple Lie algebras'' (1981)
*''Tables of dominant weight multiplicities for representations of simple Lie algebras'' (1985)
*''simpLie Users Manual: Macintosh software for representations of simple Lie algebras'' (1990)
*''Tables of representations of simple Lie algebras'' (1990)
*''Affine Kac-Moody Algebras, Weight Multiplicities and Branching Rules'' (1991)
